Description: In the Living room meeting, the visitor’s identity conflicts with the inviter information, creating two action branches: being settled in the Study and a demand to go to the Billiard room for a private talk.
Location: Living room (Living room)
Key Information:
  - Four people enter the Living room (Living room).
  - Edmund Galley explains that the visitor’s car is stuck near Quail Lane (Quail Lane), so the visitor cannot leave for the time being.
  - John Hobbes states he came because of an invitation, signed with the name Rupert Galley; Martha Galley explicitly denies that anyone in the villa has that name.
  - Recorder’s note: Person No. 4 mentions “brought a bottle of wine,” and the recorder speculates this may correspond to the wine bottle broken in a later “04-” scene (speculation).
  - Recorder’s note: The system supports setting a nickname for a numbered character via the command “name 1 John Hobbes,” and the “name” command can be used to view assigned nicknames.
  - Person No. 9 says they need to wait for their daughter to arrive before starting; Edmund Galley directly says “she probably won’t be coming,” prompting Person No. 9 to press for details.
  - Damian Maseko asks where Annie Beaumont (Annie) is; Person No. 4 says Annie Beaumont does not want to come to the Living room and expresses dissatisfaction about having to keep staying in the house.
  - Martha Galley agrees to let John Hobbes stay the night and explicitly arranges for him to spend the night in the Study (Study), while asking Damian Maseko to come along to help.
  - Person No. 9 demands that Edmund Galley go to the Billiard room (Billiard room) to talk one-on-one, emphasizing that he must come.
  - It ends by stating that everyone leaves the Living room.
Characters:
  [Martha Galley (Martha)] Person No. 5, one of the residents present, responsible for hosting and arranging.
    · Asks whether Eve Dauer (Eve) came with Edmund Galley.
    · Explicitly states that there is no one in the villa named Rupert Galley.
    · Introduces the names of those present (Victoria Maseko, Helen Dauer, Tony Dauer, Edmund Galley, Damian Maseko).
    · Agrees to let John Hobbes stay the night and arranges for him to sleep in the Study (Study).
    · Asks Damian Maseko to accompany them to help with the arrangements.
  [Edmund Galley (Eddie)] Person No. 6, one of the villa residents.
    · Says he brought a new visitor.
    · Explains that the visitor’s car is stuck near Quail Lane (Quail Lane), so the visitor cannot leave for the time being.
    · Directly states that Person No. 9’s daughter probably will not be coming.
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Introduces himself and explains that he came because of an invitation.
    · Says the inviter is named Rupert Galley and asks whether anyone present has heard of him.
    · Requests to stay one night before the weather improves.
    · Accepts Martha Galley’s arrangement to spend the night in the Study (Study).
  [Person No. 9] One of the residents present, related to their daughter’s arrival and a private conversation arrangement. However, based on the introductions, only Helen Dauer and Tony Dauer remain.
    · Asks about the visitor’s identity.
    · Says they want to wait for their daughter to arrive before starting.
    · Immediately presses after hearing “your daughter won’t be coming.”
    · Demands that Edmund Galley go to the Billiard room (Billiard room) to talk one-on-one, emphasizing that he must come.
  [Damian Maseko (Damian)] Person No. 8, one of the residents present.
    · Asks whether the visitor is doing okay.
    · Asks where Annie Beaumont (Annie) is.
    · Accepts Martha Galley’s request and accompanies them to help settle the visitor in the Study (Study).
  [Victoria Maseko (Victoria)] Person No. 7, one of the residents present.
    · Says everything is fine and that details will be explained later.
    · Challenges the visitor’s identity during the conversation.
  [Person No. 4] One of the residents present, unnamed. However, based on the introductions, only Helen Dauer and Tony Dauer remain.
    · Mentions that the visitor brought a bottle of wine.
    · Says Annie Beaumont does not want to come to the Living room and expresses dissatisfaction about why they must stay in the house.
    · Mentions that they were invited as well.
  [Eve Dauer (Eve)] A character mentioned but not present in this segment.
    · Someone asks whether she came with Edmund Galley.
  [Helen Dauer (Helen)] One of the residents introduced by Martha Galley.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony)] One of the residents introduced by Martha Galley.
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie)] A character mentioned but not present in the Living room.
    · Is said to not want to come to the Living room (Living room).
  [Rupert Galley] The inviter’s name shown on the invitation.
    · Identified by John Hobbes as the inviter, but Martha Galley explicitly denies that anyone in the villa has that name.
